usage_note: Southwest US Spanish (Mexican-heritage) uses 'hotcakes' for pancakes, not 'panqueques'. The single highest-value brand-fit term for Kodiak in the SW market.
Breakfast. Standard and SW usage agree; sweet-and-savory morning framing works.
Pancake mix as 'harina para hotcakes' in SW. Pair with the hotcakes trap term for on-brand product naming.
Oatmeal / oats. Consistent across dialects; safe for Kodiak oat products.
Green chile is a defining SW (New Mexico / Las Cruces) breakfast ingredient. High resonance for a savory flapjack spin.
Blueberries often 'moras azules' in SW usage; 'arándanos' also understood (accent on the a).
Maple syrup: SW/Mexican usage favors 'miel de maple' over Iberian 'jarabe de arce'.
Protein, accent on the i (proteína). Diacritic is orthographic-standard.
Child (niño). Enye is semantic: niño (child) vs nino (misspelling). Exercises enye round-trip.
Whole-grain as 'integral' (harina integral). Core to the 100% whole grains claim.
'Ready in minutes' convenience register fitting the on-the-go Kodiak line.
Honorific with enye; seeded to lock a second enye round-trip case.
